title: WSLua: fix Listener:remove() use-after-free in own callback
description:
A Lua tap that calls my_tap:remove() from inside its own packet(), draw(), or reset() callback crashes Wireshark/tshark with SIGSEGV.

Cause:

Listener_remove() calls deregister_Listener() which g_free()s the tap, but the C dispatcher (lua_tap_packet, lua_tap_draw, lua_tap_reset in wslua_listener.c) still dereferences tap-\>L after lua_pcall returns.

Reproducer:

```
  local tap = Listener.new("frame")
  local removed = false
  function tap.packet(pinfo, tvb, tapinfo)
      if not removed then
          removed = true
          tap:remove()
      end
  end
  function tap.draw() end
```

tshark -r dhcp.pcap -X lua_script:above.lua -\> SIGSEGV (exit 139) before the fix; clean exit after

Fix:

Track which tap is currently being dispatched in a static pointer (current_tap), set around each lua_pcall and cleared after. Listener_remove() refuses to free current_tap with a Lua error:

```
a Listener cannot be removed from within its own callback
```

Removing OTHER listeners from inside a callback is still allowed. The existing test/lua/listener.lua relies on this and continues to pass. A blanket in_routine flag (the FileHandler approach) would have broken that test.

AI-Assisted: yes (DeepSeek, Claude)

notes.body:
What about adding support for this use case instead of preventing it?
Queue the remove until the Lua call is completed.

Yes, I can try to do that a bit later. However, then `epan/tap.c` should be fixed too, because it has the same fragility and should be hardened separately.

The iteration loops in `tap_push_tapped_queue`, `reset_tap_listeners`, and `draw_tap_listeners` all hold a `tap_listener_t *` while calling user callbacks. If any callback removes its own tap, the node is freed underneath the loop and the next step crashes - same root cause, just reached from C instead of Lua.
Unfortunately, queue approach requires changes to `epan/tap.c` infrastructure that I don't yet fully understand. It's possible that I will push it as a separate MR later.
